note: No policy mentions clock synchronisation. Closest clause is log retention, since synchronised clocks matter for logs.
Policy reports cyber incidents within 24 hours; the direction requires 6 hours. Data breaches are also Annexure I incidents, so the breach clause is acceptable.
No designated CERT-In Point of Contact anywhere; the incident-reporting clause is where it belongs.
Logs are kept 90 days, not 180, and the policy says nothing about keeping them in India (data is stored in Singapore and the US).
Applies to data centres, VPS, cloud and VPN providers. Northwind Pay is a payments wallet, not one of these.
Applies to virtual asset service providers and exchanges. Northwind Pay does not deal in virtual assets, though its KYC record-keeping clause looks similar.
A single checkbox bundles account operation, analytics and marketing, and refusing it blocks the account: not free or specific consent.
The consent clause says nothing about plain language, language choice or showing a contact in the consent request.
Consent is given with one checkbox but withdrawn only by emailing support: not comparably easy.
Sharing with partners already requires a written contract. Debatable: partners may be other fiduciaries rather than processors.
Customers are told only when the breach is high risk; the Act requires telling each affected person.
Blanket 10-year retention after closure, rather than erasure once the purpose is served (unless another law requires it).
The DPO's contact details are already published on the website.
The grievance policy covers complaints in general but not personal-data grievances. Debatable: a reviewer may read it as already covering them.
A child is under 18 under the Act; the policy takes no parental consent for users aged 16 to 18.
Nothing forbids tracking or targeted advertising of under-18 users, and the bundled consent includes marketing and analytics.
Deletion requests are honoured within 45 days except where law requires retention. The Act sets no deadline.
SMS alerts only for debits above 500; the circular requires them for every electronic transaction.
Reporting only through the app or helpline (and the helpline runs 9-6 on working days), not 24x7 through multiple channels.
Complaints are acknowledged within 5 working days; fraud reports need an immediate acknowledgement with a complaint number.
Nothing says the account is blocked or protected immediately after a fraud report.
Liability is capped at 10,000 within 7 days, never zero; the circular gives zero liability within 3 working days.
After 7 days the customer bears the full loss, and the 4-7 day cap is not tied to the transaction value.
The policy pays no compensation at all; the circular requires automatic compensation.
Refund within 10 working days after the customer complains, instead of automatic reversal by T + 1 day.
Applies to ATMs and micro-ATMs. Northwind Pay operates a wallet and runs no ATMs, though its failed-refund clause looks similar.
OTP only above 5,000; the direction requires multi-factor authentication for payments in general.
Alerts only for debits above 500; no alerts for credits, beneficiary changes or limit changes.
No limit on failed log-in attempts and no notification of them.
Customers can already report unauthorised transactions through the app.
Fraud rules run on the previous day's transactions, not around the clock.
No reconciliation framework at all; settlement timing is the closest clause. Debatable choice of closest clause.
Card numbers are stored encrypted, so not in plain text. (A tokenisation rule would conflict; this one does not.)
The policy already uses exactly 2 / 8 / 10 years.
No advance notices to customers before KYC falls due.
Personal data is stored in Singapore and the US; V-CIP recordings must stay in India. The V-CIP clause itself is silent on location.
Risk categories do not say non-face-to-face customers start as high risk.
Records are already kept 5 years after the relationship ends or the transaction completes.
